blocks.text: BFS explores a tree or graph by examining all nodes at the current level before the next level. Visiting a zoo whose enclosures are joined by paths: start at the entrance (the start node) and put it in a queue; visit the enclosure at the front of the queue, find its neighbouring enclosures and enqueue them; move to the next enclosure in the queue and repeat; when the queue is empty, every enclosure has been visited.

blocks.prompt: In the zoo method, why is a queue used rather than a stack?
blocks.explanation: A queue visits enclosures in the order they were discovered, so nearer enclosures are seen before farther ones, level by level.

items: BFS: start node in a queue; dequeue, visit, enqueue neighbours; stop when the queue is empty.
